question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x).$ Then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡8$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{3}{2x{ln}^{2}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x))^{2}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot {(-{u}^{-1})|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\cdot {(\frac{1}{u})|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡{2}^{3}}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡{2}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(-\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$
